acceptance: One canonical renderer-safe token source defines the closed foundation and exposes no host capability or secret-bearing data
Semantic color pairs meet frozen machine-checked WCAG AA contrast thresholds and never encode status by color alone
Primitives preserve native semantic HTML and accessible names; interactive status and buttons support keyboard, disabled, loading, and error semantics without redundant roles
Focus treatment is always visible for keyboard use, bypasses mouse styling, respects reduced motion, and uses scalable typography
Raw color, spacing, radius, typography, and motion literals are rejected outside the canonical token source except documented structural data
The conformance checker fails closed on token bypass, unknown tokens, invalid contrast, invalid primitive semantics, and renderer authority drift
Existing connection projection and frozen unprivileged shell semantics remain unchanged and tests cover hostile token and primitive inputs
Native SpecGrain verification binds the WorkPacket to observed evidence with zero issues
Canonical closeout advances only KX-P03-S02-T01 scope

minimality.rationale: The canonical architecture names a new packages/ui-system authority and no design-system implementation exists; use existing TypeScript and Node test tooling without adding a framework or runtime dependency.

requirements: The renderer remains unprivileged and can access no direct host capability; design primitives never widen the preload bridge or create authority.
Accessibility constraints are structural and machine-tested, including semantic elements, accessible names, focus visibility, reduced motion, non-color status meaning, and contrast.

outcome: Establish one renderer-safe design-token authority, a minimal semantic primitive set, machine-tested accessibility constraints, and fail-closed design-system conformance without workspace-feature implementation.
rationale: P03-S01 has no separate canonical exit task and both macro tasks are PROVEN; the registry authorizes KX-P03-S02-T01 as the sole NEXT unit. S03.2 requires Kernux tokens, primitives, typography, an accessibility baseline, and lintable design constraints over the proven unprivileged Electron/React shell without host authority or later workspace features.

risk.recovery: Revert the bounded UI-system, conformance, renderer-integration, and frontier changes and keep KX-P03-S02-T01 at NEXT; no daemon or kernel state is created

scope_in: A single TypeScript-owned token module defining frozen primitive, semantic, status, focus, spacing, typography, size, radius, border, surface, and motion tokens; deterministic contrast pairs and reduced-motion behavior
Minimal renderer-agnostic semantic primitives for accessible status, button, surface, and visually hidden content using native elements and explicit props without a generic component framework
A repository-native design-system conformance checker that fails closed on token bypass, invalid semantic token references, inaccessible primitive markup, and renderer authority drift
Focused deterministic tests for token completeness, contrast ratios, primitive semantics, disabled/loading/error states, keyboard focus behavior, reduced motion, and hostile token/style inputs
Renderer consumption limited to proving the system against the existing shell without implementing later layout, tabs, command-bar behavior, or project-rail behavior
Persist fresh ContextSources and WorkPacket before implementation and require byte-identical pinned replay
scope_out: No adaptive pane framework, tabs, splits, docking, layout persistence, project management, command-bar behavior, timeline, artifact viewer, search, CLI, Design Mode, or Privacy Inspector
No new npm dependency, component framework, runtime package, donor code, packaging, signing, auto-update, or release artifact
No privileged host authority, bridge channel, filesystem/network/process capability, or renderer ambient Node access
No design branding service, runtime cloud cost, or provider-specific token layer
title: KX-P03-S02-T01 - Kernux design system foundation
